And Mr. Borovcanin allowed me to film everything that we can see, so one should thank him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'm sure somewhere in there there's an explanation for why that material doesn't appear on your raw footage, but I don't see it. Also what I don't see is -- on your raw footage, is the footage that you shot of the Muslim prisoners at the white house on the balcony. That does appear in the Studio B footage but can't be found on the raw footage that you provided the Office of the Prosecutor in 2006. I know that you've testified about this before, so can I take it that your explanation for that anomaly is the same as it was in your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, of course that it will be lacking in your sense of the word, but can you please quote to me any other source that was more useful for this Tribunal than my materials? And you also forgot to say that later on I submitted to the Tribunal the VHS version of the original TV show from Studio B which has gone missing, so you should ask the authorities and those who are in power in Studio B, How did it happen that it had gone missing? I was lucky that people in Canada would preserve the report, because the Serbs in Canada also attacked me in 1995 and 1996 and 1997 because of this report. I sent it -- or, rather, I took it personally, because I was a guest in 1996 in Canada and I had submitted this version to them and I had completely forgotten about it, but God seemed to have sent this tape, so you have -- the only thing that is relevant, as it was edited immediately and whatever was of any value so as to be included, was included in the poorly filmed report from the professional aspect, but rather important from the historic aspect as it turned out. At the moment, I didn't have this thought on my mind, this dimension. So it's lacking, but that's most that you ever had at your disposal at this Tribunal. I'm not a superhuman, and this is the maximum that I could have done, really, frankly, and sincerely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to ask you for a reference in the cross-examination for that part of the video, not the Kravica warehouse, but the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There's no reference during the course of the cross-examination. It's just a follow-up to what the witness gave to a question I put to him that was grounded in the cross-examination. So I asked him about what was missing from the footage, and he mentioned, in his answer to that, to the Kravica footage, the white house footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Petrovic, you've mentioned efforts made to seize this VHS recording of the footage that you made. I want to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's P1337. For the Court, this is not on my re-direct examination -- on my list of exhibits for re-direct examination, but it -- I'm raising it now because it flows directly from the witness's previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, are you tendering the document we have on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7398 shall be assigned Exhibit P2236. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would kindly ask you, this really accedes the framework of the cross-examination. All the questions being put by Mr. Vanderpuye, this is all evidence from other cases, and I don't see why he's doing that now and why there is a precedent being made in terms of the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On page 43, lines 12 to 18, Mr. Vanderpuye gave a reference, the second time, to that part of your cross-examination. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, Dr. Petrovic, have you ever seen this footage -- [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to see where this document is being mentioned, and I would like to know where the data is being referred to in this document. Did I talk about a cassette, movement of a cassette, how the cassette was obtained? You can get questions to -- answers to this, but I just want to say that this accedes the boundaries of the cross-examination. I never spoke about any cassette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you referring to the document on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Mr. President. A cassette is being mentioned here that I did not mention at all during the cross-examination, its movements or anything relating to it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, perhaps Mr. Vanderpuye can clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I can, Mr. President. What the witness answered in respect of my last question, I think it was either the last or the second-to-last question, specifically was the fact that efforts were made to seize a missing VHS cassette containing the footage which he shot. The document I have relates precisely to that issue, and that relates, indirectly as it may be, to General Tolimir's question on cross-examination concerning the nature and the scope of the material that was shot by Dr. Petrovic. He asked him whether all of the footage that he shot of Kravica was all of the footage there was. I asked him about that, he gave an explanation. He also added in his explanation that there were efforts that were made to seize the VHS recording or that the VHS recording had mysteriously disappeared of footage that he shot. And here we can see a document that addresses precisely the efforts and -- and addresses the issue concerning the raw footage that Dr. Petrovic shot and also concerns the seizure of that material. So I put it to this witness, first, whether he's familiar with the document, and then I can explore, I think briefly, the pertinent issues that are responsive to the questions before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If the goal of Mr. Vanderpuye is to expose some other persons to unpleasant things in the way that he is exposing Mr. Pirocanac to them, and it was ridiculous when I said during the cross-examination that there is an attempt to try him for verbal offences, then I have nothing against Mr. Vanderpuye proceeding in the way that he is. I would just like to note that this is not within the framework of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, Mr. Vanderpuye explained that this should be a follow-up question to the last answer of the witness. You can see mentioning of the VHS version of the original TV show from Studio B. That is on page 47, lines 17 to 18. No, it's not your turn to -- to get the floor. Do you see that? Do you recall that, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it would be the same as if I were to say that it was relevant that the war in Yugoslavia preceded the war in Libya. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Dr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, no, please, I would like to get a response from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I guess the argument is that it's an irrelevant issue. I think it is directly relevant to the question of -- without admitting the document, let me just frame it this way: General Tolimir asked this witness whether the three seconds of video that he shot that appear on the Studio B footage, that is, the Kravica warehouse sequence, is all of the material that he shot of the Kravica warehouse. I've asked him two things. One: Whether or not he had the opportunity to shoot additional footage as would be indicated in the statement of Borovcanin who says that they stopped at the warehouse. And the second question is this: On this document, and I'm not using it at this point, I'm just referring to part of it, it says: "Raw material with footages, many of which have never seen daylight, is on a video-tape owned by Zoran Pirocanac." This is referring to the raw material that is not on the Studio B recording, which is what we've seen, which is where the Kravica warehouse footage appears. Then they talk -- then the document goes on to explain other information concerning that video material. So the extent of my question only relates to whether or not there is material other than the footage than what we can see on Studio B, as per either from this document or any other information that this witness may know about. So it's directly, directly, related to General Tolimir's question and it bears upon this witness's -- first of all, his veracity, and it also bears upon the completeness of the information that he has provided to the Trial Chamber and the footage itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, could you please help us to understand your re-examination, especially the relation between the Studio B version of the footage, the raw material, and the so-called VHS version you are now obviously dealing with. What is the relation between these different kinds of -- the video footage and the relation to that part of the cross-examination you were referring to? Judge Nyambe wants to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Vanderpuye, we might be helped, as a Chamber, if you gave us a reference in the accused person's cross-examination where this particular issue has been referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As I -- as I said before, the reference is -- the reference is derived from the accused's question to the witness about the completeness of the Kravica warehouse footage, which is where I began. If you bear with me for one moment, I can give you the page number. It starts at page 14491, line 23, and goes through 14492, line 12. And, in particular, the question was as follows: "Thank you, Dr. Petrovic. Please, we'll move on to what you filmed or what you saw. As I indicated earlier on page 67, 21, you talked about footage which registered in front of the door of the hangar in Kravica a certain number of bodies, and you estimated that the number was roughly around 20 bodies. You were asked several questions in relation to that. "Can you please tell us whether these were all the bodies which you filmed at the location in Kravica or is there another footage? Thank you." And the answer was: "All bodies ... I personally saw were filmed. But let me repeat once again, my footage hardly lasts 3 seconds. It's maximum of 3 seconds while passing by Kravica." And so on and so forth. The question was whether or not there is another footage as relates to the events that we've seen in Court, the Studio B issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye and Mr. Tolimir, the reference Mr. Vanderpuye gave us and read out from the transcript during cross-examination is a sufficient reason to continue the cross-examination [sic] in relation to the question if there's another footage. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. All right. I think it has disappeared from the ... oh, no, it is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Dr. Petrovic, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I was given the document four years ago, after finishing my testimony by Mr. Nicholls. Maybe it was Mr. McCloskey. But I think that it was Mr. Nicholls. I was quite surprised about that, and I can explain how you actually went in completely the wrong direction on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to ask you some questions, if you don't mind. First, you can see here that this is a centre for information and propaganda activities of the VRS Main Staff, and it's signed by chief, Colonel Milutinovic. And it refers to, in particular, your footage. You can see that. I'd like to direct your attention, if I could, to the paragraph which I read out, in part, a few moments ago, which begins, I think it's the third paragraph: "Raw material with all footage" [sic] "many ever which have never seen daylight is on a video-tape owned by Zoran Pirocanac." Again, that's you; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It says: "He is currently in Canada ..." Do you recall if you were in Canada on or about the 22nd of June, 1996?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there that summer. I don't know the dates. I can find them in my old passport.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It says: "He is currently in Canada and the tape it held by his long-term associate, journalist Vesna Hadzivukovic in Belgrade, who was entrusted with the tape." Do you know Vesna Hadzivukovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. She was a part of my team in the Bina agency where I worked for a period of time. It's a news agency. B-i-n-a, Bina.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did she have custody of a video-tape with the raw footage that's indicated in this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that, although entrusted, that word. Well, you could say it like that. I didn't take it to Canada with me. I left it to a -- with a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The journalist being Vesna Hadzivukovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. She had that function in our agency, even though she did not complete any journalist education or journalist schools. In our agency, though, she did have that function, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me take you to the fifth paragraph, which says: "Vesna Hadzivukovic and her boyfriend, formally a member of the RSK press centre, Zeljko Radovanovic, want to get rid of the tape and hand it over to VRS as soon as possible." Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I saw this for the first time when Mr. Nicholls gave it to me. If it's relevant for you what they said about wanting to -- well, I don't know why they would want to get rid of it. Why did they take it on in the first place? I mean, it's a completely stupid thing. I would like to say something about the letter by Mr. Milutinovic as well. I mean, the whole thing is a bit stupid. I would like to explain to you where you went wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me finish with this and then you can explain to me. Further on in this document it says: "Since the tape does not belong to them," meaning Radovanovic and Hadzivukovic, "they have to obtain a written receipt from the VRS saying that the tape was seized in order to be able to justify the procedure to Pirocanac when he returns." It then says: "I have already told them to say ... everyone who is interested in the tape that it was handed to VRS Main Staff Information Service and, if necessary, they can refer to me." Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Mr. Vanderpuye. Based on this, you can only conclude that these are associates of that service, because that person is from Bosnia. Actually both of them hail from Bosnia. So they receive a cassette and then they have to explain that it was seized and then they take it away. I mean, this really lacks any seriousness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It then says: "I will maintain contact with them until the hand-over." And that's obviously Colonel Milutinovic who's saying this. "Whoever collects the tape will have to take a written request for seizure of the tape stamped by the VRS ... Whoever collects the tape has to go with a receipt." I want to show you another document. It's P1338.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You read the last part of this document to the witness without putting a question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's true, Mr. President. And I don't have a question about the last part of it. It was just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not necessary because we have it in evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'm showing you now -- well, it's self-titled, and it says: "Authorised official of VRS security body." And it says: "Receipt for temporarily seized items" [sic], and it refers to a civilian, Vesna Hadzivukovic from Belgrade, and it talks about one video-tape. It says: "The object is seized from her and the objects were received by naval captain Ljubisa Beara." First, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I did see this one. But it's still completely senseless, just like the one before it. Would you like me to tell you why?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I'd just like to know what you know about the document. You haven't seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing it. But the Army of Republika Srpska cannot officially seize anything in Belgrade from anyone. I mean, really, this is an absolutely senseless thing. It's a different state. You can withdraw this document completely. Do you understand what you put up here? It's -- somebody is saying something. People coming to Belgrade to seize something to a different state. I mean, it would like you going from Holland to the United States to seize a document. I mean, you could try to do that. I'm a little bit disappointed. This is not what I expected, but we can analyse it --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Dr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can analyse the first document as well, because my honour is at stake here, and we're talking about military manipulation here right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about your honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, no, may I interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you tell me, why are you referring to Belgrade in your last answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is logical. That person lives in the centre of Belgrade. She's a citizen of the Republic of Serbia. By origin, she hails from Bosnia because her father is from there, who was a non-commissioned officer. But she lived in Belgrade. And then Colonel Milutinovic appears and Beara who are supposed to seize that material officially, right in the middle of Belgrade. I mean, this really makes absolutely no sense at all. Mr. President, this is a fake document. It's a fabricated document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you help me to explain that, that you say it was seized in Belgrade? How can you draw such a conclusion from this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a telephone number in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm talking about this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the place of residence of that person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm talking about this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, all right. All right. Yes. Well, we see that the military post number is a Sarajevo military post number. The object was received by the -- naval captain Ljubisa Beara. As far as I can recall, he was a military intelligence officer. And he seized from a civilian from Belgrade a cassette that she herself had offered up, together with her boyfriend, as it was stated previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Once again, what is the basis of your conclusion that this was seized in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the text of the previous document. If you permit me, I will explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You were asked about this document and then you said: "People coming to Belgrade to seize something to a different state." That was your answer. I would like to understand this answer on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. President. Thus, let's proceed step by step. The cassette - and I don't know which cassette it is - the cassette is in Belgrade. The document, the first one and the second one, arrives from Republika Srpska, which is a different state, which cannot do anything in the territory of Serbia, in Belgrade. Belgrade is in Serbia. And then they come. It doesn't even state in the document that the person went to Bosnia. But you cannot seize something officially in Belgrade on the basis of a document from Sarajevo. This is what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You can seize something in Bosnia on the basis of a document that's from Sarajevo, can't you? I think you can answer that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and you can see that this document refers to --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- Articles 221 and Articles 151 and 154 of the Criminal Law on Procedure; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In a different state. I don't see where this was seized, and that's why I believe it was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... well, in the state -- in the state where this document would have been issued; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it clearly from it. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and you don't see clearly on it that this shows that the seizure took place in Belgrade either, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no mention of Belgrade in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's right. And so when you say that it's impossible for this document to be legitimate because the seizure happened in Belgrade, that's just a speculation on your part, isn't it, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we can all read the document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's be fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... show us on this document where it says that the seizure occurred in Belgrade. Show us that in support of your conclusion that that's where it happened. And it's time for our break. Maybe you can find it during that time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a vicious circle. I will show you, if you allow me to use the previous document, that that is senseless, but you're not allowing me. I cannot give you an answer, because you put me against the wall this way, and there's no need for that. Mr. Milutinovic, you received his document, is a man who forbade myself and all journalists from Serbia or from abroad to come to the area of Srebrenica. He told me, If you go in there, Pirocanac, I will arrest you. That's why I went with Mr. Borovcanin. So this is the man who sent this document. I don't know why this document was not presented four years ago. You had it then, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You can't put such a question to Mr. Vanderpuye. Let's see, again, P2236.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, you referring to the previous document, I think. It's P1337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If that is the document that the witness is referring to, let's see that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we have it. The telephone number that you were referring to, Doctor? 011-458-705. And it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just to -- we need to clarify which is the number of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I have it as P1337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was my mistake. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You said that can you see on this document that the seizure took place in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. If you allow me, I'll read the last paragraph. "Vesna and Zeljko are in Belgrade" - I do not know their address - "but they can be reached at telephone number 011-458-705." 011 is the call number for Belgrade, at the time still part of Yugoslavia, and Sarajevo was 071. So they are in Belgrade. And then it says: "And arrangements can be made for the tape to be handed over." So they are calling them in Belgrade for the purpose of a hand-over. "We don't know where the hand-over will be. I will still maintain contact with them until the hand-over." It's still the same. That's obvious. So who's going to be going to collect the tape, this whoever person? We'll have to take a written request. Where will he have to go then? To Sarajevo? I hope you understand this. Everything here indicates that the people will go to their apartment in Belgrade to take the tape and that, in the meantime, they would be in contact. But this is not of great importance to me. I'm interested in this cassette and what happened to it. But this is some kind of military to-do. The only reference that we have is a phone number in Belgrade. And it says also, whoever collects the tape, meaning the person who will go to get it. But in essence this is some foul play. These are some people working for the military. I never worked for the military. Let me remind you: Mr. McCloskey, after the first questioning, and you had all my details, stated that I never worked for any police or military structures. This is an affront to me. This was done by people who maybe were not journalists but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should be very careful to use words like "provocation" and "affront." You are a witness. And you are questioned. And I put a final question before the break to you: What is the difference between hand-over and seizure? Or is it the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this last quotation I read is something that leads me to believe, and I hope that in explanation I was convincing, leads me to believe that they are doing this on a voluntary basis, because obviously they are somehow linked up with Mr. Milutinovic, the person who had forbade me from entering Srebrenica. I can glean that, reading the text. So it was a voluntary hand-over. They got in touch with the army and not the other way around. Still, it's obvious that they are in Belgrade, not Bosnia, and Republika Srpska is a different state here. And all this is something I knew nothing about at the time because I was in Canada then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is the source of your estimation that this hand-over took place in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me to read it again, I don't know whether it was translated to you, because there it is stated Vesna and Zeljko are in Belgrade. I don't know their address, but they can be reached at telephone number such and such. It's a Belgrade phone number. And arrangements can be made for the tape to be handed over. It says: For the tape to be handed over. I will still maintain contacts with them until the hand-over. Until.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How can you draw a conclusion from this text that the hand-over took place in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm basing it on logical conclusions. We do not have enough information. Maybe the Prosecution has additional information, but this is the only conclusion I can make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't want to hear any more -- anything about that. Thank you very much. We must have the second break now, and we will resume at 6.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Dr. Petrovic, you mentioned, when we looked at the other document - I think it was 1338, P1338; that was the receipt - that you recognised the name Beara on that document, and you indicated that he was with the intelligence service of the VRS. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you know that naval captain Ljubisa Beara was directly subordinated to General Tolimir in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I didn't know about that fact at the time. I knew that he was a member of the army, but I didn't know what his position was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to take you to another area. You indicated, at page 14492 in a question put to you by General Tolimir concerning the prisoners in Sandici, and he asked you, at line 24 of that page, or beginning at line 24 of this page: Please tell us, later on, on page 67 you said -- actually, you said on page 57 ... that according to your estimate in the Sandici meadow there was a total as many people as could fit into one single bus. Can you please clarify this a little bit for us so that we would have a clearer picture of that? Thank you. Because you were asked by cross questions about one and the same subject." I think he means direct? And your answer is, and this is at page 14493: "General, sir, it's the same as with the dead in front of the hangar in Kravica; it's just my personal estimate. Once again I say that -- perhaps it's not appropriate," and you make a reference to a football match and basically that it's a running estimate. So then you say, at line 14: "So perhaps around 100 people or less. Today I think that would be about" [sic] "100 people." So I wanted to ask you some questions based on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment, please. The record was not complete. After line 14 of page 66, you clarified that Mr. Tolimir was not referring to cross but to examination-in-chief. That was missing here on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I think what I'd like to do is to go into private session because there's another area of cross-examination which overlaps with this and I think it would be appropriate to do that. If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. This is the statement of the person that I just referenced in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what I'd like to do is to take you to page 5 of the English. And I'll need some help to find it in the B/C/S. It should be ERN ending -- wait a minute. Bear with me one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We need to go two pages ahead in the English. Okay. And I think I'll need some help to find it in the B/C/S. Okay. It should be page 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is already on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Oh, great.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here, this individual talks about what transpires at the meadow. And he says that a Serb soldier with a red bandana called those who were born in 1979 and 1980 to stand up. About ten stood up, but he didn't. Two other individuals told him to get up, and he said he replied that he was older, but they told him that he looked younger. And he says: "I told them I could not leave my father. But they just grabbed me and made me stand up." And that he'd never heard or seen of these two individuals again. He was the last to stand up. And he says the soldier with the red bandana told him to go faster as the youngsters started walking towards the road. "One of the soldiers sitting on the tank cursed the soldier with the red bandana when he let me go." And then he says, in the next paragraph, that on the asphalt road he got into a civilian blue truck with a yellow canopy and he says there were approximately 20 women that had from Potocari. Some of the women mentioned that they were in Sandici, outside Kravica. And a Serbian soldier had stopped this truck on the road "and we, the 11 youngsters, boarded the truck. The truck stopped in Vlasenica for approximately ten minutes and locals threw stones at us but also cigarettes." And he further describes what happens to him after this. Is this consistent with your recollection of how you saw -- or what you saw happen to these youngsters, as he calls them, while you were at Sandici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, from this perspective 16 years later, and I, of course, have not read this document, but I will repeat, I say that Mr. Borovcanin's order that all these children - I remember that there were at least ten of them - around ten or so, as far as I can remember, was to stop the convoy and to have these youngsters board the buses or vehicles. So this corresponds somewhat to that. But I did not see what was happening in the buses. I didn't come near because it was a bit down the road, as far as I can remember, that the traffic was stopped, and I simply filmed that. I didn't film this, but if I did, perhaps we would be talking differently now. I don't know what else to tell you by way of my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go back one page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I just wanted to ask you one thing on this -- about one thing on this page. And that's on the -- about the fifth paragraph -- well, next-to-last paragraph, where he states that he was in a group of approximately -- well, approximately a thousand people. And this is where -- the area where they were gathered. And that would be in the area of Sandici. He describes -- he describes that he saw a lot of baggage, rucksacks, and personal belongings along the track, which I think means path, as we approached the main road. And then he was directed to a partly destroyed house on the right side close to the asphalt road. Now, you were asked some questions by General Tolimir about how many people were on the meadow, and you said it was about a bus-load full, I think. About 100. Do you accept that there were substantially more than 100 people in that meadow on the day that you were filming there, if not at the time that you were filming there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, at the moment or moments when I was there, some of my footage shows quite a wide view of the entire meadow on the other side of the road. In my footage, I think even if professionals were could count, there couldn't be more than 100 people. I did not spend the whole day. I came there in the afternoon and then I left. I was going around quickly, there was a lot of shooting, and you forget that I risked my life in order to film that. At the moment when I filmed that, at the moments that we spent there, I depicted all the people in the footage. There was no reason for me to depict 100 and hide 900. How could I do that? Because in my footage, if you have look at the reportage, you can see the entire space. But I did not spend 24 hours in the area. These were just minutes, 10 or 15 minutes. I don't know anymore. But it was short because the whole area along the road was unsafe. The fighting was not finished on that day nor on the following day. And this is something that is often forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If this witness boarded a bus at the time, when Dr. Petrovic was looking, how could he have seen one thousand people than if Dr. Petrovic saw and filmed only 100 people? He shouldn't be asked about something that could have happened earlier or later. We could ask about something that happened earlier, but Mr. Vanderpuye should ask him could he have seen anything different from what the other witness did see. Could they have seen the same event at the same moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness provided his answer. Mr. Vanderpuye, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I remind that we are approaching the end of today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I've got maybe two minutes more. I will tender the document that I have first, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is P933. It is marked for identification, if I'm not mistaken. Do you recall the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe it was marked for identification because it was the subject of a -- of a 92 bis application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I just wanted to ask you, Dr. Petrovic, are, you aware -- first of all, did you discuss the number of prisoners that were at the Sandici meadow, at the Kravica warehouse, with Mr. Borovcanin any time during the period of time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, that is also possible. Though in my earlier statements I believe I said that I do not remember us discussing that. Everything was still in progress. I was concentrated on what I was filming. And he had his military activities to take care of. Perhaps he told you in one of his statements that perhaps we did discuss that. What I can remember now is that in the reportage which I published in the newspapers, I described in quite some detail how the operation which began on the 4th or 5th of July was carried out and conducted from the military point of view, and it's possible that he provided me with some general information, for example, from which axes the Serbs were coming, where were the Muslim positions, because this is mountainous terrain. This was fighting in the mountains. It was quite difficult. And I remember that there was this part in the interview which you quoted on several occasions, but I really cannot tell you exactly. If you could help me by referring me to some of his statements, I don't think there's anything disputed if we did discuss that. But if we did, then the main subject was this part of my future report, namely how the operation was conducted, I think up to the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to know if you can recall it. If you can't, that's fine. Let me ask you this: Are you aware that Mr. Borovcanin reported on 13th of July that his forces had captured or received surrendered Muslim prisoners of about 1500 between the 12th and the 13th of July, 1995. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You will understand, Mr. Vanderpuye, that I'm a civilian and a journalist. He had already done a lot. And this is a military piece of information that he had no reason to import to a civilian, regardless of how well-known the civilian may have been at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I just want to put up on the screen, if I could, 65 ter 5338.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then we'll be finished, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a report headed "Ministry of Interior, MUP, Special Police Brigade," dated 13 July. And you can see it's sent to Pale Police staff, Vogosca Police staff and the Special Police Brigade at Janja. If we go to the bottom of this document, you can see, and it's the second page in the English, that it's issued by Ljubisa Borovcanin who is the deputy commander of the Special Police Brigade. And in the second-to-last paragraph you can see that it reads that: "In the night between 12 and the 13 July, the armed Muslim group launched an attack in the direction of Konjevic Polje. In the combat that lasted several hours and which continued throughout the day, the enemy sustained a loss of 200 soldiers who were killed, and we captured, or had surrender to us, around 1500 Muslim soldiers, and" [sic] "the number increases by the hour." You weren't aware of these circumstances, I take it, while you were staying with Mr. Borovcanin for the 40 hours that were in the area on the 13th and 14th of July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Vanderpuye. All this happened before my arrival, and Mr. McCloskey wrote that I had nothing to do with either military or the police. So, in other words, this is not a piece of information to be given to a civilian, so I didn't know about this. This comports with my story.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to know is if you were aware.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that concludes my re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 5338 shall be assigned Exhibit P2238. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Vanderpuye. You will be pleased, sir, to hear that this concludes your examination here in this trial. You may now return to your normal activities, and the Chamber would like to thank you that you were able to come to The Hague and to testify here in this trial. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, in the afternoon, 2.15 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of May, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
